title: Patterson's 49 Turns the Trophy Upside Down
title_candidates: Patterson's 49 Turns the Trophy Upside Down
A Round for the History Books at Praia D'El Rey
The Novice Who Nearly Broke the Record
theme: A near-stranger to the leaderboard produces a career-defining round that rewrites the record book and flips the Trophy race in one afternoon.
tone: wry, deferential awe at an outlier performance, with the course's teeth played for dark comedy underneath
opening_hook: Somewhere between the dunes of Praia D'El Rey and the clubhouse bar, John Patterson — a man with precisely one previous TEG round to his name — produced the sort of scorecard that usually arrives with an asterisk and a drugs test.

round_story.subject: John Patterson's 49-point round, the second-best total in TEG history to date, built on a front-nine rescue and a back-nine avalanche of points
round_story.why_it_matters: This is the best round of the day by a distance, and it belongs to a player with barely any TEG history to speak of, making it the natural anchor for the report
round_story.shape: He bleeds eight shots across holes 4-6 and looks set for another quiet day; a birdie at the 7th halts the slide; from there he piles up seventeen points across holes 9-13 and another fourteen across 15-18 to finish on 49, the second-highest points total ever recorded in the competition.
headline_candidates: A Round for the History Books
round_story.standfirst: A man with only one previous TEG round to his name carded the second-highest points total in the competition's history, recovering from an early wobble to do it.

race_story.subject: Jon Baker's one-point overnight Trophy lead evaporates as a ragged middle nine drops him to third, ten adrift of the new leader
race_story.why_it_matters: The Trophy race changed hands overnight and Jon Baker, not John Patterson, is the one whose week this story really belongs to — he did nothing wrong except stand still while someone else sprinted past
race_story.shape: He starts the day a single point clear at the top of the TEG 9 Trophy; a joyless stretch without a net par at holes 5-7 and a quadruple bogey at the short 14th arrest any progress while Patterson catches fire elsewhere on the course; he ends the round in third place, ten points off a lead he never had to actually lose a duel for.
headline_candidates: The Lead That Didn't Survive Saturday
race_story.standfirst: Jon Baker's one-point cushion atop the TEG 9 Trophy is gone, undone less by anything Patterson did to him directly than by a ragged middle nine of his own.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker, a day after his worst-ever gross round, posts a personal-best round, a personal-best gross score, and a new course record at Praia D'El Rey
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A genuine turnaround story grounded in his own course history — nine shots better than his previous best here, the day after carding an eleven at the same hole that undid him again briefly on Saturday
discovered_storylines.shape: Friday's 43-over horror show, including an eleven at the 14th, is still fresh; he steadies himself through the front nine before a wild quadruple-bogey nine at the 10th threatens to derail things again; he recovers to finish on 44 points and 27-over gross, both personal bests, and a course-best at Praia D'El Rey by nine shots.
headline_candidates: From Worst Ever to Personal Best
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A day after carding the worst gross round of his TEG career, Alex Baker returned to Praia D'El Rey and beat his own course record by nine shots.

discovered_storylines.subject: Praia D'El Rey's par-4 9th and short par-3 14th combine to wreck four separate scorecards across the field
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A reminder that the course, not just the players, is shaping this TEG — and it accounts for the mandatory blow-up beats the other two stories don't cover
discovered_storylines.shape: The course's reputation for coastal drama precedes it; Gregg Williams cards a sextuple-bogey ten at the 9th and Stuart Neumann a quadruple there too, while both Alex Baker and Jon Baker card quadruple bogeys at the short 14th within the same round; four separate blow-up holes later, the course's teeth are the quiet through-line of the day.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: The par-4 9th and the short 14th combined to wreck four separate scorecards, a reminder of why this course is treated with such respect.

race_state_note: The Green Jacket and Wooden Spoon pictures are largely unchanged at the extremes — David Mullin's lead grew from two to seven, Stuart Neumann's gap to safety from eight to fourteen — while the Trophy race has been completely reshaped.
